title: Development of a Patient-Reported Outcome Measures to Detect Perioperative Symptom Burden Following Major Abdominal Surgery for Cancer
summary: Surgery is often the treatment of choice for cancers of the digestive system. After surgery, the patients’ condition is assessed by clinicians subjectively. Patient-reported outcomes measures have been shown to improve symptom management in hospitalized patients with advanced cancer. The present study describes the development, feasibility, and testing of a daily questionnaire for symptom monitoring in patients following major abdominal surgery for cancer.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of anus and anal canal
Malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile ducts
Malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified parts of biliary tract
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥ 18 years
2. major abdominal surgery for gastrointestinal malignancies
defined as:
3. Minimally-invasive or open surgery
4. Written informed consent
5. Ability and willingness to respond to questionnaires
Exclusion criteria:
1. ASA > 4
2. Impaired mental state or language problems
